codex-juror.first_action: Tap the knight-and-hydra suggestion, then tap “Make it!” to create a playable game.

losses.note: After tapping “Make it!” at 2.6 seconds, the first accepted game input is at 5.0 seconds.
Dodge and Strike are labeled, but the wind-up and opening are not visually obvious enough to time my taps.
I am already out of lives after 4.8 seconds, with only 2% progress and no clear explanation of what I mistimed.

codex-juror.verdict: I would stop at 10 seconds because the premise is clear, but the short defeat gives me little guidance or incentive to retry.

opus-juror.first_action: I would tap the first suggestion card ("A knight fights a three-headed hydra…") and then tap "Make it!" to see what the app generates.

losses.note: The game drops me straight into a fight; the only guidance is the vague "Dodge the wind-up, strike in the opening" line, and the Dodge/Strike buttons sit low next to an unexplained Quick/Full detail toggle, so I can't tell when to press which.
I'm dead after 4.8 s with 1 point and 2% progress, and the clear "Tap right to strike, tap left to dodge" hint only shows up on the game-over screen, after it would have helped.
The Quick/Full detail toggle over a grey blank area at the top of the results screen looks unfinished and doesn't say what it does.

opus-juror.verdict: I'd give it one more try, because going from one sentence to a playable game in about 3 seconds is impressive, but losing that fast with the controls explained only after death makes the gameplay feel punishing and thin.

opus-player.first_action: I'd tap the knight vs. three-headed hydra card and then hit the big orange "Make it!" button.

losses.note: The game drops me straight in with Dodge/Strike buttons and a vague 'dodge the wind-up, strike in the opening' line, and I can't tell what a wind-up looks like from that tiny red dino-looking 'hydra'.
I lost all 3 lives in 4.8 seconds with 1 point and '2% of the way', and the 'tap right to strike, tap left to dodge' tip only shows up after I'm already dead.
The 'Quick / Full detail' toggle and the 'Change one thing' button sit right on the game and pull my eyes away from the fight.

opus-player.verdict: I'd probably hit Try again once since it loaded super fast and the knight looks cool, but dying in under 5 seconds without getting how the timing works makes me likely to bail back to TikTok after that.

codex-juror.first_action: Tap “Surprise me” to get a game idea.

losses.note: The suggestion cards are mostly below the screen and obscured by the bottom navigation.
The game appears at 5 seconds, but the tester’s first accepted tap is at 5.8 seconds.
Dodge and Strike are visible, but I cannot tell what signals an incoming attack or an opening.

codex-juror.verdict: I would stop after 10 seconds because the round ends with zero points before I understand the attack timing.

opus-juror.first_action: I'd type a one-sentence game idea, or tap "Surprise me", then tap "Make it!".

losses.note: The suggestion cards are pushed below the fold and hidden behind the Make/Play bar, with only "castle gates." peeking out, and the grey placeholder text looks like it's already filled in, so I can't tell if I need to type.

I drop straight into a knight-vs-hydra game while the instruction text, a cut-off yellow banner and a Quick/Full detail toggle all compete for attention, and the Dodge/Strike buttons sit under that toggle, so I don't know what the opening or wind-up looks like.
After about 6 taps I lost all 3 hearts in 4.8 s with 0 points, and only now does it say "tap right to strike, tap left to dodge", on a dimmed, washed-out overlay where even Try again looks disabled.

opus-juror.verdict: Probably not: the one-sentence-to-game idea is clear and fast, but I died with 0 points before I understood the controls and the faded game-over screen doesn't make me want to retry, so I'd move on to the next project.

opus-player.first_action: I'd tap "Surprise me" or "Make it!" to see what game it makes, because the suggestion cards are mostly hidden behind the bottom nav bar.

losses.note: The suggestion cards are cut off under the Make/Play bar, so all I can see is "castle gates." and I don't know there are ready-made ideas to tap.
The game throws me straight in with a Quick/Full detail toggle, Dodge/Strike buttons and an instruction about "wind-up" and "opening", and I can't tell when to dodge or strike.
I'm dead after 4.8s with 0 points even though I was tapping, and it only tells me "tap right to strike, tap left to dodge" after I've already lost, so it feels unfair.

opus-player.verdict: Maybe one more try, since making a game from one sentence is cool and it loaded fast, but losing with 0 points before I got how the controls work would make me quit soon if the second run goes the same way.

codex-juror.first_action: I would click “Tap to play” to try the game already displayed.

losses.note: The game timer already shows 1.0 seconds while I am still locating the Dodge and Strike controls at the bottom.
I have lost all three lives after lasting just 4.8 seconds, reaching only 2% before getting comfortable with the game.

codex-juror.verdict: I would stop at 10 seconds because the immediate defeat makes learning the game feel too costly for a quick review.

opus-juror.first_action: I would hit the big yellow "Tap to play" on the preview, or type a sentence and press "Make it!", since the headline "What do you want to play? Say one sentence" makes the idea clear right away.

losses.note: There are two main buttons at once, the yellow "Tap to play" on a preview that already shows a running timer and the orange "Make it!", and the suggestion cards are cut off at the bottom of the left column, so I can't tell which path is the intended one.

The game starts with a hydra fight instead of the fox-and-dog idea in the text box, and the controls are only two small "Dodge (Down)" and "Strike (Space)" pills at the bottom, so it takes me a moment to work out the timing mechanic.
I lose all 3 lives in 4.8 s with 1 point and "2% of the way", and the control hint only shows up on this death screen, which feels punishing rather than inviting.

opus-juror.verdict: I would probably press "Try again" once, because going from a sentence to a playable 3D game in about 2 seconds is impressive, but dying within 5 seconds with the controls explained only afterwards makes it likely I'd move on to the next project.

opus-player.first_action: I'd hit the big yellow "Tap to play" button on the crystal game since it's already right there, before bothering to type anything.

losses.note: There are two big buttons fighting for me, a yellow "Tap to play" on the demo and an orange "Make it!" next to a text box, so I'm not sure if I'm supposed to play or make something first.
I get dropped straight into a knight vs. hydra fight with a tiny instruction line, and I have to figure out the Dodge/Strike keys at the bottom while it's already going.
I'm dead with 0 lives and 1 point after 4.8 seconds, and "2% of the way" makes it feel unfair and kind of pointless.

opus-player.verdict: Maybe one more try, because making a game from a sentence in about 2 seconds is cool, but losing all 3 lives in under 5 seconds feels cheap, and I'd probably swipe back to TikTok if the next run went the same way.
